key_insight: Interface orientation tunes heat transfer in lateral MoSe₂/MoS₂ heterostructures: extrapolated infinite-length thermal conductance is 473 MW/m²K for armchair versus 387 MW/m²K for zigzag interfaces.
engineering_relevance: Choosing armchair interfaces could improve heat dissipation in lateral TMD nanoelectronic and optoelectronic devices.
method: Train a deep learning interatomic potential with DeePMD-kit on DFT data.
Use non-equilibrium molecular dynamics to compare armchair and zigzag interfaces.
Simulate cell lengths of 10–40 nm and extrapolate conductance to infinite length.
evidence_signal: The potential closely matches DFT energies, forces, and phonon dispersions; armchair conductance is higher at every tested length, with greater phonon spectral overlap at 300 K.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based results; experimental validation and sensitivity to real-interface defects remain unestablished.
paper_title: Orientation-Tunable Interfacial Thermal Conductance in Lateral MoSe2/MoS2 Heterostructures: A Deep Potential Molecular Dynamics Study
